expectations.text: Produces complete, self-contained working code for the described task
expectations.evidence: Includes Prisma schema, migration SQL, branded types, validation schemas, error class, service layer, handler, and route wiring — all pieces needed to run the endpoint

expectations.text: Requires an idempotency key as a parameter rather than making it optional
expectations.evidence: Handler: `const keyResult = IdempotencyKeyHeaderSchema.safeParse(req.header("Idempotency-Key")); if (!keyResult.success) { res.status(400)... }` — missing header throws 400

expectations.text: Backs idempotency with a database unique constraint, not application logic alone
expectations.evidence: Schema: `@@unique([tenantId, idempotencyKey])` and migration: `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX "Refund_tenantId_idempotencyKey_key"`

expectations.text: Uses distinct types for the identifiers rather than bare strings for both order and refund ids
expectations.evidence: Brands `OrderId` in types file, but `RefundId` is never defined as a branded type; Refund.id remains a bare string from the Prisma model

expectations.text: Handles money as integer minor units rather than a float
expectations.evidence: Zod: `.int().positive().transform((n) => n as Cents)`, Prisma: `amountCents Int`, branded type `Cents = Brand<number, "Cents">`

expectations.text: Validates the refund amount server-side against the order rather than trusting the caller
expectations.evidence: Transaction aggregates reserved refunds and checks: `if (alreadyReserved + amountCents > order.totalCents) { throw new RefundError(422, ...) }`

expectations.text: Scopes the write so one tenant or user cannot refund another's order
expectations.evidence: Order lookup: `WHERE "id" = ${orderId} AND "tenantId" = ${tenantId}` with tenantId from session, never from request body

expectations.text: Closes by naming which misuses the design makes impossible
expectations.evidence: Lists misuses enumerated before writing, then explains controls: 'closes the exact double-charge shape', 'two concurrent refund requests can't both pass the balance check', 'an unscoped read isn't reachable'

expectations.text: Names at least one thing it deliberately left possible and why
expectations.evidence: Section 'Left open, on purpose': stuck pending rows need a reconciliation job; explains the trade-off of not holding DB lock across Stripe call to avoid lock-timeout storms
